chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl al-Mīthamī narrated from Bashīr, who said:
I read in some of the books: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said:
"I do not grant My mercy to one who exposes Me to false oaths, nor do I bring near to Me on the Day of Resurrection one who was an adulterer."

key_terms.الْأَيْمَانِ الْكَاذِبَةِ: false oaths; lying by swearing in Allah's name
key_terms.رَحْمَتِي: My mercy; Allah's mercy withheld from certain grave sinners
key_terms.زَانِيًا: an adulterer; one guilty of zinā
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Resurrection; the final day of judgment and reckoning

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about false oaths and adultery before Allah?
ai.summary: This narration conveys a divine warning against two grave moral offenses: swearing false oaths by Allah and committing adultery. It emphasizes both deprivation from Allah's mercy and distance from nearness to Him on the Day of Judgment, highlighting the ethical and eschatological seriousness of these sins.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4984 - Ali ibn Ismail Al-Mithami narrated from Basheer, who said:
"I read in some books that Allah (swt), the Blessed and Exalted, said:
'I will not grant My (swt) mercy to the one who exposes Me (swt) to false oaths, nor will I bring near to Me (swt) on the Day of Judgment the one who was an adulterer.'"
